examples.title: API 500 Errors - Full System Flow
examples.description: Complete debugging workflow showing how ANY model can perform multi-step reasoning with tool integration

input.user_request: Our production API is returning 500 errors for 5% of requests. The issue started after yesterday's deployment. Available Tools: file_read, grep, code_analyzer.
input.context: Production Node.js API, microservices architecture, PostgreSQL database
constraints: Cannot restart service during peak hours (9AM-9PM)
Must identify root cause within 2 hours
input.goal: Identify root cause and propose fix with minimal downtime

steps.name: Understand Problem Scope
steps.thought: User reports 500 errors on 5% of API requests. This started after deployment. Need to establish severity and impact.
steps.why: Cannot investigate without understanding scope and business impact
steps.action: Analyze error rate, identify affected endpoints, assess user impact
steps.expected_output: Problem definition with severity assessment and affected endpoints
steps.validation: Error rate quantified, affected endpoints identified, business impact assessed
steps.actual_output: 5% error rate = ~500 errors/hour at current traffic. Primary affected endpoint: POST /api/orders. Business impact: Users cannot complete purchases.
steps.fallback: If error rate unclear, estimate based on typical traffic patterns

steps.name: Collect Error Log Data
steps.thought: To identify error patterns, I need actual log data. User mentioned production API, so I should check the main error log.
steps.why: Cannot analyze error patterns without the raw error data
steps.action: Retrieve the most recent error logs from the production API
steps.expected_output: Last 1000 error entries from production API with timestamps, endpoints, error codes, messages
steps.validation: File exists, readable, contains at least 100 error entries, timestamps in chronological order
steps.actual_output: Retrieved 1500 error entries from last 24 hours. 850 entries for POST /api/orders with 500 status code.
fallback: Use sample error data and note limitation
Request user to provide error log excerpt

steps.name: Identify 500 Error Patterns
steps.thought: Now I have error logs. I need to find all 500 errors and group them by type to identify patterns.
steps.why: Pattern identification reveals root cause categories and common characteristics
steps.action: Search for all 500 errors in the log data and categorize by error message
steps.expected_output: List of all 500 errors for POST /api/orders with context, grouped by error message type, count of each type
steps.validation: All 500 errors captured, context sufficient, grouping accurate, error types clearly identified
steps.actual_output: Found 850 entries. Top error: 'Connection timeout to database' (680 occurrences, 80%). Other: 'Invalid request body' (120), 'Payment gateway timeout' (50).
fallback: Use manual search through log data
If no 500 errors found, expand search to all errors
Note that pattern identification may be incomplete

steps.name: Analyze Deployment Correlation
steps.thought: 80% of errors are database connection timeouts. User mentioned it started after deployment. Need to check what changed.
steps.why: Correlation with deployments strongly suggests code or configuration changes as root cause
steps.action: Compare error timeline with deployment history to identify correlations
steps.expected_output: List of recent deployments with timestamps, versions, and changes. Correlation with error spike at deployment time.
steps.validation: Deployments retrieved, timestamps align with error spike, changes are documented
steps.actual_output: Deployment v2.3.4 at 2026-08-05 14:00. Changes: Updated database connection pool from 20 to 10 connections, added new order validation. Error spike began at 14:05.
fallback: Check git history if deployments.log unavailable
Proceed with error pattern analysis only

steps.name: Verify Root Cause Hypothesis
steps.thought: Hypothesis: Connection pool reduction from 20 to 10 caused timeouts under load. Need to verify current pool size and usage.
steps.why: Must confirm hypothesis before proposing solution
steps.action: Check current database connection pool configuration and active connections

tool_parameters.command: grep -r 'connection_pool' api/config/ && ps aux | grep postgres | wc -l

steps.expected_output: Current pool size configuration and count of active PostgreSQL connections
steps.validation: Pool size confirmed as 10, active connections count retrieved
steps.actual_output: Connection pool configured to 10. Current active connections: 15 (exceeds pool size).
fallback: Try alternative command to check connections
Accept hypothesis based on circumstantial evidence

steps.name: Propose Solution
steps.thought: Root cause confirmed: Connection pool exhaustion. Pool size reduced from 20 to 10, but load requires 15+ connections. Solution: Increase pool size back to 20-25.
steps.why: Need to provide actionable recommendation that addresses identified root cause
steps.action: Synthesize all findings into clear, testable solution with implementation steps
steps.expected_output: Primary root cause, proposed solution, implementation steps, rollback plan, success criteria
steps.validation: Solution addresses root cause, implementation steps clear, success criteria measurable, rollback plan defined

actual_output.solution: Increase connection pool size from 10 to 25
actual_output.rollback_plan: Revert to connection_pool.size=20 if errors persist

steps.fallback: If solution unclear, propose diagnostic steps to gather more information

key_findings.description: 80% of 500 errors are database connection timeouts
Connection pool was reduced from 20 to 10 in deployment v2.3.4
Current active connections (15) exceed pool size (10)

recommendations.action: Increase database connection pool size from 10 to 25

lessons_learned: ANY MODEL can effectively perform multi-step debugging when provided with clear step structure
Tool integration enables data collection and verification
Self-dialogue in each step makes the reasoning process transparent
Fallback paths ensure robustness even when some tools fail
Intermediate result tracking creates audit trail for debugging
why_this_works: Each step has a single, clear purpose
Tool calls are explicit with exact parameters
Fallbacks provide alternative paths if tools fail
Self-dialogue explains the reasoning behind each action
Intermediate results build upon each other
